subject: Liability cap carve-out for trade secrets — proposed evidence & preservation workflow
messages:
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@novamed.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Gina Park <gina.park@novamed.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Liability cap carve-out for trade secrets — ask ahead of PO

Logan —

Thanks for the quick follow-up on the pilot. Legal at NovaMed flagged a requirement we need to resolve before I can route a PO: our security team wants an explicit carve-out to Redwood's liability cap for proven trade-secret exfiltration and will need an evidence-preservation workflow spelled out in the contract (forensics, chain-of-custody, timetables).

High level asks from our side:
- Carve-out language in the MSA/Order Form that removes the cap for damages arising from willful misappropriation of trade secrets.
- A defined preservation & forensics process (who we notify, timeline for suspending backups, access for a mutually agreed forensics vendor).
- Confirmation on liability for third-party subpoenas and injunction costs (we need clarity whether Redwood will indemnify in limited instances).

I attached our internal checklist (PDF) for evidence preservation. Can your legal team propose redline language and a practical operational process we can accept? We're trying to avoid protracted back-and-forth — if you can share proposed MSA text and a one-page runbook by EOD Wed we can keep the procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, IT Security
NovaMed Health

Attachment: evidence_preservation_checklist.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@novamed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 17:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Liability cap carve-out for trade secrets — ask ahead of PO

Daniel —

Appreciate the clarity and the checklist. Looping in Laura (legal) and Evelyn (Delivery) so we can align contract language with an operational playbook.

Quick answers before the formal redline:
- We are open to a narrowly tailored carve-out for proven, willful trade-secret misappropriation by Redwood personnel or agents. We cannot accept an unlimited, open-ended carve-out; it will need to be scoped (e.g., direct damages and reasonable remediation/forensics costs).
- We can commit to a defined evidence-preservation runbook: 24-hour initial acknowledgement, hold on routine deletion/retention purges for 30 days, and coordination with a mutually agreed independent forensics firm.
- On subpoenas/injunctions: we generally cooperate, and in certain cases where legal process imposes extraordinary costs we will evaluate indemnity on a case-by-case basis; Laura will propose tighter language.

Action plan: Laura will send a redline against the current MSA and Order Form with specific wording for a trade-secret carve-out and a short operational runbook. Evelyn will add delivery constraints (retention holds, access windows for investigators). Can you confirm the vendor you prefer for forensics (if you have one), otherwise suggest that we pick a neutral third party?

I attached the current MSA so Laura has a starting point.

—Logan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: NovaMed_MSA_current.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@novamed.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Liability cap carve-out for trade secrets — proposed redline and runbook

Daniel / Logan —

Thanks — I reviewed NovaMed's checklist and drafted both: (1) a narrow MSA carve-out and (2) an evidence-preservation runbook suitable for attachment to the Order Form. Key points in the redline (attached):

- Carve-out scope: removes the liability cap only for "willful and material misappropriation of a customer's trade secrets" where (i) customer provides prima facie evidence to Redwood, and (ii) a court or arbitrator ultimately determines misappropriation occurred, or the parties agree in writing to the findings of an independent forensics firm. The remedy is limited to direct compensatory damages and reasonable remediation and forensic investigation costs.
- Consequential damages: we preserve the general limitation on consequential damages except where excluded above; punitive and exemplary damages remain carved out by applicable law.
- Forensics protocol: 24-hour initial response, preserve storage snapshots and logs for 30 days, preserve related KVs and model cache segments on an expedited hold, and allow a single mutually agreed independent firm to conduct forensics with a scoped access plan and confidentiality protections.
- Indemnity language: Redwood will cover reasonable costs of a mutually agreed independent forensic investigation where the independent firm finds misappropriation attributable to Redwood. For third-party subpoenas, we will cooperate and absorb routine legal assistance costs but will reserve rights to seek contribution if exposure exceeds normal litigation costs.

Evelyn added operational constraints so the runbook includes timelines for evidence export, encryption key handling (if applicable), and secure delivery of forensic artifacts. Rishi — I included suggested Order Form counters (pricing/hold periods) so Procurement can close the PO without a deviation.

Daniel — please let me know if we need to widen the carve-out (e.g., to include gross negligence) or tighten the evidentiary standards. If NovaMed is comfortable we can incorporate the redline into the current DocuSign envelope (link below) and I can prepare a short side letter describing the operational runbook.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: NovaMed_MSA_redline_v3.docx
Related link: https://app.docusign.com/DocID?d=SN-4821

From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@novamed.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Gina Park <gina.park@novamed.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 20:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Liability cap carve-out for trade secrets — acceptance pending one tweak

Laura / Logan —

Thanks — the redline looks strong and the runbook addresses most concerns. One small ask from our CISO: tighten the preservation window language from 30 days to 45 days for evidence and logs where an incident affects long-tail backups. Also, we want the independent forensics firm to produce a findings memo that is admissible under the rules of evidence — if Redwood is comfortable with that deliverable we can accept the recommended carve-out and move forward.

We also confirmed we don't need a blanket indemnity for subpoenas as long as Redwood confirms it will prioritize NovaMed's data preservation requests and will not perform disposal during an active preservation hold. If you can update the redline for (a) 45-day preservation for affected artifacts and (b) a clause confirming Redwood will not purge related artifacts during an active hold, we can complete the PO approval and sign.

I'll attach the DocuSign envelope id (text file) for reference; please keep the side letter short and operational.

Cheers,
Daniel
Director, IT Security, NovaMed Health

Attachment: DocuSign_Link_SN-4821.txt
